learning_outcomes.text: Graduates possess broad knowledge about model building, mathematical description, simulation, and properties of systems and signals.

Graduates have detailed knowledge of model building and simulation of physical-technical systems. They have an overview of simulation-based development methods and are familiar with exemplary modeling languages and simulation tools.

Graduates can model and analyze simple technical systems. They can apply block diagram-oriented simulation tools. They know advanced simulation tools and modeling languages and their application areas.

syllabus_topics: Model building: introductory examples, basic concepts, basic principles of model building, model validation, numerical aspects
Signals and systems: concepts, classification of systems and signals, Laplace transform, dynamic behavior, transfer functions, sampling
Continuous modeling and simulation, introduction to control loops
Discrete modeling and simulation with applications in digital systems (e.g., networks, computing systems)
assessment_rules: The graded examination performance is chosen by the lecturer from a written project report (7-12 pages), an exam, or a media project report (5-10 pages). The ungraded examination performance consists of experimental work, comprising approximately 5 experiments of 90 minutes each.
